Sampling variances with a given informativeness and logit variance

Source: R/algebra-shapes.R
shape_profile.Rd

Builds sampling variances whose reliability profile at a given between-site standard deviation has exactly the informativeness I and the logit variance V, in one of four shapes. These are the profiles of the simulation study of Lee (2026, Appendix F).

Usage

shape_profile(
  J,
  I,
  V,
  shape = c("even", "bimodal", "concentrated_precise", "concentrated_noisy"),
  sigma_tau = 1
)

Arguments

J

Number of sites, an integer of at least 1.

I

Informativeness of the profile, a number strictly between 0 and 1.

V

Logit variance of the profile, a number of at least 0. With J = 1 it must be 0.

shape

Shape of the profile: one of "even" (the default), "bimodal", "concentrated_precise" or "concentrated_noisy". See Details.

sigma_tau

Between-site standard deviation at which the profile has the informativeness I, a positive number.

Value

A numeric vector of J sampling variances.

Details

The variances are \(v_j = \tilde v\, e^{x_j}\) with \(\tilde v = \sigma_\tau^2 (1 - I) / I\) and deviations \(x_j\) of mean 0 and mean square \(V\), so that the logits of the reliabilities have mean \(\mathrm{logit}(I)\) and variance \(V\). The shapes of the deviations:

  • "even": equally spaced, a ladder of variances that is even on the log scale.

  • "bimodal": two groups of \(\lceil J/2 \rceil\) precise and \(\lfloor J/2 \rfloor\) noisy sites, which are not symmetric when \(J\) is odd.

  • "concentrated_precise": \(k = \lceil J/5 \rceil\) precise sites at \(-\sqrt{V(J-k)/k}\) and the other \(J - k\) at \(\sqrt{Vk/(J-k)}\), so a fifth of the sites have reliabilities far above the rest.

  • "concentrated_noisy": the mirror image, with \(k\) noisy sites.

At V = 0 all four shapes give equal variances. The sites come in the order of their deviations as listed: from precise to noisy, except for "concentrated_noisy", whose noisy sites come first.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

v <- shape_profile(J = 40, I = 0.3, V = 1, shape = "concentrated_precise")
S <- site_reliability(se2 = v, sigma_tau = 1)
kl_centroid(S)
#> [1] 0.3
logit_moments(S)
#>    V rho3 
#>  1.0  1.7
